name: Linear Algebra True/False
description: True or false questions compiled from all Linear Algebra quizzes and midterms

questions.question: You can never have more free variables than basic variables in a system of equations.
options: True, because pivot columns always outnumber free columns in any consistent system
True, because free variables are always bounded by the number of equations in the system
False, because a system like x1 + x2 + x3 = 1 has one basic variable and two free variables, showing free variables can outnumber basic ones
False, because any overdetermined system automatically produces more free variables than basic ones
questions.explanation: This is false. For example, x1 + x2 + x3 = 1 has one pivot (one basic variable, x1) and two free variables (x2 and x3), so free variables can easily outnumber basic ones.

questions.question: Any system of equations has a solution.
options: True, because every matrix can be reduced to RREF, which always produces at least one valid solution
True, because the zero vector is always a valid solution to any linear system
False, because systems with more equations than unknowns are always unsolvable regardless of coefficients
False, because a row in RREF of the form 0 = 1 indicates an inconsistency, so no solution exists
questions.explanation: This is false. An inconsistent system has no solution. A row that reduces to [0 0 ... 0 | c] with c not equal to 0 in RREF signals a contradiction, meaning the system has no solution.

questions.question: An example of a linear combination of v1 and v2 is 3v1.
options: True, because 3v1 equals 3v1 + 0v2, and zero is a permitted weight in a linear combination
True, because any scalar multiple of a single vector automatically spans the same subspace as both vectors together
False, because a linear combination of two vectors must include both vectors with nonzero coefficients
False, because 3v1 is a scalar multiple, which is a distinct operation from a linear combination
questions.explanation: This is true. A linear combination allows any real weights, including zero. Writing 3v1 + 0v2 is a perfectly valid linear combination of v1 and v2.

questions.question: In some cases, a matrix may be reduced to more than one matrix in reduced row echelon form (RREF) using different sequences of row operations.
options: True, because row operations are not unique, so different sequences can lead to different final matrices
True, because swapping rows before pivoting can produce a different RREF with the same row space
False, because non-square matrices have no unique RREF and always yield multiple valid reduced forms
False, because the RREF of any matrix is unique regardless of which sequence of row operations is applied
questions.explanation: This is false. The RREF of a matrix is always unique. Different sequences of row operations may take different paths, but they all produce the same final RREF.

questions.question: A vector b is a linear combination of the columns of a matrix A if and only if the equation Ax=b has exactly one solution.
options: True, because if b is in the column space of A, the system Ax=b always has exactly one solution
True, because a consistent system always has a unique solution when b can be written as a column combination
False, because b is in the column space of A if and only if Ax=b has at least one solution, which need not be unique
False, because Ax=b must always have infinitely many solutions whenever b is a linear combination of the columns of A
questions.explanation: This is false. A vector b is a linear combination of the columns of A if and only if Ax=b is consistent, meaning it has at least one solution. The system may have a unique solution or infinitely many solutions.

questions.question: A matrix is invertible if and only if det(A) is not equal to 0.
options: True, because a nonzero determinant confirms the columns are linearly independent and the transformation is bijective
True, because the determinant equals the trace, and any matrix with a nonzero trace must be invertible
False, because a matrix can be invertible even when its determinant is zero, as long as all rows are nonzero
False, because determinants are only defined for 2x2 matrices and the invertibility criterion cannot be generalized
questions.explanation: This is true. A square matrix is invertible if and only if its determinant is nonzero. A zero determinant means the columns are linearly dependent and the transformation collapses space, so no inverse can exist.

questions.question: If Ax=0 has a nontrivial solution, then A must have at least one pivot column.
options: True, because a nontrivial solution to Ax=0 requires at least one constrained variable, which implies a pivot column must exist
True, because any matrix with a consistent homogeneous system must have leading entries, which are pivot positions
False, because the zero matrix has no pivot columns yet Ax=0 holds for every nonzero vector x, providing nontrivial solutions
False, because nontrivial solutions to Ax=0 only arise when A has more unknowns than equations, preventing any pivots from forming
questions.explanation: This is false. The zero matrix is a counterexample: it has no pivot columns, yet Ax=0 for every vector x, so any nonzero x is a nontrivial solution.

questions.question: In a linear combination c1x1 + c2x2 + ... + cnxn, the weights c1, ..., cn can all be zero.
options: True, because setting all weights to zero produces the zero vector, which is a valid output of a linear combination
True, because a linear combination requires all weights to sum to zero, making all-zero weights the standard form
False, because at least one weight must be nonzero for the expression to qualify as a linear combination
False, because all-zero weights would imply the vectors are linearly dependent, making the combination undefined
questions.explanation: This is true. The definition of a linear combination places no restriction on the weights. Setting all weights to zero is valid and produces the zero vector.

questions.question: It is possible for 5 vectors in R^4 to be linearly independent.
options: True, because linear independence depends on the directions of the vectors, not the dimension of the space they live in
True, because if each of the 5 vectors has a distinct largest entry, they are guaranteed to be linearly independent
False, because a 4x5 matrix is overdetermined and therefore always produces a dependent set of column vectors
False, because in R^4 at most 4 vectors can be linearly independent, so any set of 5 must be linearly dependent
questions.explanation: This is false. In R^n, any set of more than n vectors is automatically linearly dependent. Since we are in R^4, a set of 5 vectors must be linearly dependent.

questions.question: A basic variable is one corresponding to a pivot column in the coefficient matrix.
options: True, because every variable in a linear system is basic unless the augmented matrix has an inconsistent row
True, because basic variables are identified by pivot positions, which mark the leading nonzero entries in each row after row reduction
False, because basic variables correspond to free columns in the coefficient matrix, while pivot columns contain bound variables
False, because pivot columns only appear in invertible square matrices, so basic variables cannot be defined in general
questions.explanation: This is true. During row reduction, pivot columns identify the basic variables. Every variable corresponding to a pivot position is a basic variable; all remaining variables are free.
